answer: Epoch Drift Scoring: each agent identity keeps a rolling behavioural fingerprint (call timing, task mix, counterparty graph) compared across epochs. An identity whose fingerprint drifts past a fixed distance from its own history loses credit weight, like a current forced through a narrow canyon. Fresh sybils start with no history, so they sit on a small island of low trust until many epochs pass. Attacker cost: sustaining N credible identities requires N parallel consistent histories, an ocean of upkeep, not one cheap clone burst.
